#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from PBS
# The PBS request for 1 node with 12 processors for a single command is
# interpreted as a request for 1 task with 12 CPUs.
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -c 12
#FLUX: -t 24:00:00
#FLUX: -o /Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.out

#
# --- Omitted PBS options and explanations ---
#
# -l vmem=94gb
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct batch script directive for memory.
#   Performance implication: Without this very large memory constraint, the job
#   is almost certain to be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory,
#   potentially causing it to fail with an out-of-memory error.
#
# -j oe
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into a single output file by default
#   when no error file (-e) is specified. This is consistent with the output file
#   redirection in the original script.
#
# -M briochemc@gmail.com and -m abe
#   Omitted. Flux core does not have built-in support for email notifications via
#   batch directives. This functionality may be provided by site-specific
#   plugins or wrappers.
#
# -e $HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.err
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file specified
#   by the -o directive. The separate error file path is ignored.
#

# Load the julia module
module load julia/1.1.0

# Go to the root folder on katana
# NOTE: $HOME is used to construct paths. The script assumes this will resolve
# correctly in the Flux execution environment.
cd $HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization

# Set DataDeps environment variable to download without asking
DATADEPS_ALWAYS_ACCEPT = true

# Run it!
julia src/run_TimerOutputs_w0.jl

issues: As correctly noted in the script's comments, the original PBS memory request of 94GB (`-l vmem=94gb`) was omitted. This is a catastrophic omission for a long-running job. Without this very large memory constraint, the job is almost certain to be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, leading to an out-of-memory failure.
The line `DATADEPS_ALWAYS_ACCEPT = true` contains a shell syntax error due to the spaces around the equals sign. This will cause the script to fail at runtime with a 'command not found' error.

The script requests 12 CPU cores (`-c 12`), but the efficiency of this depends entirely on whether the Julia script `src/run_TimerOutputs_w0.jl` is multi-threaded and can utilize all 12 cores. If it is single-threaded, 11 cores will be left idle, leading to significant resource waste.

The script is extremely non-portable. It uses the `$HOME` variable to construct hardcoded absolute paths for the output file and the working directory. It will fail for any other user or if the project directory is ever moved.

The job will fail at startup if the absolute path specified for the output file (`$HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/`) does not already exist or if the user does not have write permissions to it.
